_comment: Shared contract for the ![image](...) destination grammar, which exists in two
languages: the dashboard composer's producer `mdImageDest` and its inverse
`mdImageDestToPath` (website/src/utils/fileTokens.ts), and the backend's
producer `kiro_crew.uploads.markdown_image_dest` with the outbound scanner
`kiro_crew.messaging.outbound_files.iter_local_refs` as its inverse. A row the
backend writes must render in the dashboard, and a row the composer writes
must resolve on the way out to a channel, so both producers must spell each
`path` as exactly `dest`, and both inverses must read `dest` back as exactly
`decoded`. The FRONTEND test (website/src/test/fileTokens.test.ts) and the
BACKEND test (test/test_slack_one_renderer.py) each walk every case, so an
escaping change on either side fails that side's suite instead of silently
breaking the other side's round-trip.
`decoded` is the inverse's output, not the original `path`: slash
normalisation of a Windows path is one-way by design, so a drive-letter or
UNC path decodes to its forward-slashed spelling.
`outbound_local: false` marks a destination the outbound scanner does not
treat as a local file at all -- a `//host/share` spelling is a remote
reference there (an SMB probe nobody asked for), so it yields no local
reference. The frontend inverse still decodes it, because it only renders.
`legacy_bare` pins the other half of the provenance rule: an UNWRAPPED
destination is never percent-decoded, because it is either inside the
pass-through-safe alphabet (decode is the identity) or pre-existing history
whose `%20` is part of the on-disk name.

cases.name: a POSIX uploads path inside the safe alphabet passes through unchanged
a Windows drive path is spelled with forward slashes
a UNC path is forward-slashed too
a space in a Windows path wraps the destination
a space and parentheses wrap a POSIX path, parentheses unescaped
a percent sign is written %25 inside the wrap
angle brackets are backslash-escaped inside the wrap
a space and angle brackets together
a POSIX backslash is a filename byte, escaped inside the wrap
the safe alphabet is ASCII, so a non-ASCII letter wraps
a literal %20 in a name survives the wrap as %2520

legacy_bare.name: an unwrapped legacy destination is preserved verbatim
